item.title: State Republicans and Democrats Launch Bills for Affordability
item.description: Many New Yorkers around the state have felt steep prices in their wallet, especially when healthcare and utility bills were due. On February 24, two different announcements were made in the state capitol as Democrat and Republican lawmakers pushed aid to all of New York.

item.title: Eyewitness Sports Scoreboard for Wednesday, February 25
item.description: The winter sports season is nearing the end, and high schools and colleges all over the Mohawk Valley are still fighting for banners and glory! The hunt for championships continues, and you can keep up with all of the action on the Wednesday edition of the Eyewitness Sports Scoreboard!

item.title: Molinaro announces campaign for 102nd Assembly District
item.description: Marc Molinaro, former head of the Federal Transit Administration, has announced that he will be returning to New York State politics for the 2026 election season.

item.title: Six people arrested after three-month assault investigation in Clinton
item.description: Oneida County Sheriffs have arrested six people for their parts in an altercation in the village of Clinton in November.

item.title: Youth Justice Fund could divert teens from court, jail
item.description: New York lawmakers and youth advocates are pushing for a $50 million investment in community groups to support young people, as the state has failed to distribute most of the money allocated for the Raise the Age law.

item.title: New York Planned Parenthood clinics may close without aid
item.description: Reproductive health advocates rallied at the New York State Capitol to lobby legislators to fill budget gaps caused by federal policies and to secure funding for Planned Parenthood clinics, which provide a range of services including contraception, prenatal care, and gender-affirming care.

item.title: Gillibrand wants $130B tariff refund
item.description: New York Democratic leaders are demanding that President Donald Trump refund billions of dollars to small businesses and consumers after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled his global tariffs were illegal.

item.title: New York Lawmakers Look to Help New York Homebuyers
item.description: According to the state, in the 2020s, New York has been at the lowest end of homeownership rates compared to the other states. Lawmakers in the capital are racing to turn that around.

item.title: Federal judge approves plan for Syracuse Catholic church to pay millions in sex abuse settlements while avoiding bankruptcy
item.description: After five years of court procedures, a federal judge approved a plan to reorganize the finances of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Syracuse, resulting in a $176.1 million settlement to be paid to hundreds of children who were sexually abused by Catholic clergy.
